LESSON: WRITING 13.5.1 CREATIVE WRITING: NARRATIVE COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.5: Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition, part of Strand 13 in Grade 7 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What makes a story memorable? 2. What is the importance of using idioms in communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on the reason creative writers use idiomatic expressions in writing,

2. explain situations that call for the use of the following idiomatic expressions: o biting off more than you can chew o own up to something o having a lot on your plate o call it a day o piece of cake o hold your tongue

3. confirm the meaning of the idiomatic expressions from print and online dictionaries,

4. practise using the idiomatic expressions in sentences,

5. plan a narrative composition based on emergency response during road crashes incorporating the 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on the reason creative writers use idiomatic expressions in writing,
2. explain situations that call for the use of the following idiomatic expressions: o biting off more than you can chew o own up to something o having a lot on your plate o call it a day o piece of cake o hold your tongue
3. confirm the meaning of the idiomatic expressions from print and online dictionaries,
4. practise using the idiomatic expressions in sentences,
5. plan a narrative composition based on emergency response during road crashes incorporating the 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 13.5.1 Creative Writing: Narrative Composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Problem Solving: It is enhanced when the learner explains situations that calls for the use of idioms.

• Creativity and imagination: It is developed as the learner undertakes tasks that encourage artistic expression of ideas while

composing narratives using idiomatic expressions.

Values:
Integrity is enhanced as the learner displays honesty when reviewing peers’ compositions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is enriched as the learner plans to write narrative compositions in groups.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Learner relates the narrative writing skill to their learning of creative writing in Kiswahili.
